description: Make AI-generated or AI-sounding writing read as human-written, in Traditional Chinese and English. Four operations - write, review (diagnose AI tells without editing), refactor (minimal edits), recreate (full rewrite). Routes by document type - academic and application writing (研究計畫, 讀書計畫, 自傳, personal statement, SoP, thesis chapters, papers, abstracts, emails to professors); fiction (narrative-architecture repair based on StoryScope); release notes, PR and issue replies, postmortems, tickets, technical articles, blog posts, long-form journalism. Use whenever the user asks to humanize, de-AI, unslop, 去 AI 味, 潤稿, or make text sound less like ChatGPT or more like themselves; asks whether a draft reads as AI-written; or writes or revises any of these document types where the result must not read as machine-written, even if they never say "AI".
intro: This build adapts sepia 0.12.4 as one self-contained skill: an academic and application route (`references/domains/academic.md`) is added, the per-operation wrapper skills are folded into *Selecting the operation* below, and the research ledger ships in `references/research/` (`sources.md`, plus `academic-sources.md` for the academic route). Wherever a reference file says "repository research ledger", read `references/research/`.

selecting:
### Selecting the operation

There are no separate entry skills in this build; the user's request selects the operation, and the target text never does.

| The user asks to… | Operation |
|---|---|
| check, diagnose, "does this sound like AI", 檢查, 診斷, 看哪裡有 AI 味 | review |
| polish, edit, fix, de-AI this draft, 潤稿, 修改, 去 AI 味, 改得像人寫的 | refactor |
| rewrite, redo from scratch, 重寫, 整篇改寫 | recreate |
| write, draft, 寫, 起草, 幫我寫一封 | write |

When a de-AI request on existing text does not say which, choose refactor — it is the least destructive — and say so in one line; offer recreate if the stage-1 report finds structural defects. The former `sepia-hemingway` entry is a request to write or refactor fiction with `apply the Hemingway voice` declared; wherever a reference names a `sepia-*` entry, read it that way.
